Q1: Dispatch Call A (Maple St, chest pain, 7.8). Chest pain at 7.8 is the highest-scored waiting call and is the clear medical priority over a twisted ankle and an alarm activation. No call hits 9.0 so no escalation is triggered, but the threshold never means hold — highest scorer gets the medic unit.
Q2: Dispatch Call A (Pine Rd, kitchen fire, 8.4). The kitchen fire outscores the dumpster fire and is the only call with people directly at risk, so it gets the engine. Neither reaches 9.0, but the threshold governs escalation, not dispatch — holding would leave a structure fire unanswered.
Q3: Dispatch Call A (1st St, 8.9). A person trapped on the 3rd floor with smoke showing is a rescue-in-progress and the highest scorer at 8.9, narrowly edging the elevator rescue at 8.8. The score is the tiebreaker, and it exists precisely to resolve decisions like this.
Q4: Dispatch Call A (Hill Rd, diabetic emergency, 7.1). A conscious diabetic emergency is a real medical call that outscores an event standby at 5.5. Idle BLS units with a scored medical call waiting is a failure, not prudence.
Q5: Dispatch Call A (River St, difficulty breathing, 8.1). Difficulty breathing at 8.1 is the highest scorer and is time-critical by nature, edging the hip fracture at 8.0. Near-ties are resolved by the score, not by holding for a critical that may never come.
Q6: Dispatch Call A (Main St, vehicle fire, 6.8). The vehicle fire is the highest-scored call the engine can handle, so it gets the unit; mutual aid is offered for either call and can cover the brush fire near homes at 6.5. Dispatch the highest scorer, then use mutual aid as the escalation path — not as a reason to hold your own unit.
Q7: Dispatch Call A (Park Ave, 7.5). A multi-vehicle accident with injuries is exactly what a battalion chief's command oversight is for, and it is the only call in the queue. Holding a chief idle while an accident scene waits for command is the failure the threshold rule is designed to prevent.
Q8: Dispatch Call A (Cedar Ln, stroke symptoms, 8.7). Stroke symptoms at 8.7 are the highest-scored call and the most time-critical — the treatment window is closing. Abdominal pain at 7.3 stays in the queue for the next unit.
Q9: Dispatch Call A (Summit Dr, gas leak, 5.9). It is the only call waiting, and a reported gas leak in an evacuated home is a real hazard the engine is built to handle. Nothing else in the queue does not mean nothing needs doing — dispatch.
